title: Data retention and deletion
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of data retention and deletion
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: The declared lifetime of stored information
The age at which removal applies
A remaining duplicate in another store

blocks.text: Record ages are6, 7, 9 days. Cache contains copies of all three.
Retain age6; delete content ages7 and9 from primary and cache under the policy. Retain only allowed audit metadata; backups need their stated expiry process.

independent_case.title: Changed independent case
independent_case.task: Fictional retention policy deletes records at age >=4 days. X is3 days, Y4, Z5. A copy of Y remains in a temporary log after its main record is deleted. Evaluate compliance.
independent_case.answer: Keep X; delete Y and Z. The boundary includes4. Y cleanup is incomplete while a copy remains in a declared storage location. Check all locations within the policy scope; do not claim global deletion without evidence.

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
This fictional retention exercise is not a statement of legal retention requirements.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: Toy policy retains session content for 7 days and deletes it when age is at least7. Audit metadata may remain for 30 days without content. Track primary storage, cache and backup policy separately.
